rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 9 (sensor_size 0.016, kp 1.8, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.1, narrow five-sensor array) is the best raced design at 403.3, up from 366.7. On the oval it finished 20 of 20 (iteration 8: 18 of 20), with line_loss_events 0.15 (0.30), max_error 0.0376 (0.0438) and progress 0.998. The s-bend improved in progress (0.55 vs 0.34) but its line_loss_events rose from 1.0 to 2.0, and it still finished 0 of 20. The slalom progress fell from 0.17 to 0.10 with line loss still at 1.0. The Evaluator's conditions for the next step are not cleanly met. The oval held or improved, so the footprint change stays. The s-bend and slalom line loss did not fall below 1.0, so the Evaluator's kp 1.6 step is not triggered.

Change. None. I resubmit the iteration 9 design unchanged (sensor_size 0.016, kp 1.8, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.1, ki 0, last_direction, sensor_weights [2,1,0,-1,-2], narrow five-sensor array). The reasons: it is the best raced design, the oval is the most reliable track, and the one remaining variable (a kp step) would be a stacked change against an unresolved s-bend result. Two single-variable tests are possible, but the race is the scored output, so I hold the proven design.

Expected result. Oval completion near 20 of 20 with line_loss_events of about 0.15 to 0.3 and max_error near 0.04. The s-bend and slalom remain the gap, with progress 0.5 to 0.6 on the s-bend and about 0.1 to 0.2 on the slalom.

Hypotheses. (a) The larger 16 mm footprint lets sensors see the line further off-centre on the oval, which is why oval line loss fell. (b) On the s-bend, the larger footprint blends readings on tight bends, so line loss rose to 2.0 even though progress improved. (c) The s-bend and slalom are sensitive to kp, and kp 1.6 would test whether the kp trend continues there. Measurements requested: completion, progress, completion_time, line_loss_events, max_error and steering_oscillation on each track, plus noise_robustness, against the iteration 9 baseline.
